item: Reference-run follow-up: the passphrase is scrubbed from the engine's words where they are made, never from field names; no passphrase minimum; a non-UTF-8 key file is refused without a byte
summary: Delta-check findings D1-D5 on #1317: the runner puts no minimum on a passphrase (the app's rule is guidance, and the store is a throwaway); the secret is applied to the child's JSON values, error tails and exception text where they are read, never to keys or to the finished report (a passphrase equal to a verdict word could rewrite the status the exit code reads); a non-UTF-8 passphrase file is refused without naming a byte; the CLI's refusal lines reduce paths to file names; the third-signal test uses a TERM-ignoring leader with a grandchild; the command sets RLIMIT_CORE to 1, not 0 (measured: a piped core handler ignores every other value, so 0 let a full dump of a process that had read the key through), and refuses before the passphrase is read when the hard limit is already 0; --plan never reads the passphrase file (a plan runs nothing and is not asked for the core limit).
